subject: error related with too big number of areas?

messages.author: 14775dca67d88966
messages.subject: error related with too big number of areas?
parts:
Hi,
I am writing in case Dr. Matzke or somebody else could help me with the following problem:

I have a dataset of 22 sp and 20 geographical areas. When I try to run DEC,DECJ,DIVA or DIVAJ models, I get the following error:
"Error in optimx.check(par, optcfg$ufn, optcfg$ugr, optcfg$uhess, lower,  :
  Cannot evaluate function at initial parameters"

I tried the same 22 sp dataset but with only 4 geographical areas (just to try with a much smaller number, to be sure that there was not another type of problem), and this worked well.

Then I relaunched the analysis with the 22 sp dataset and 15 geographical areas (which makes sense also for my study) and then it started to run, but after a while I had to stop it because it was consuming all the memory available on the computer where I launched it (300Gb). Is there a way to limit this?

So, I would like to ask whether somebody knows if there is a limitation on the maximum number of areas that BioGeoBEARS is able to handle with? Does anybody knows where if there is a solution to those errors/problems I obtained?

Any help will be greatly appreciated, thank you,
Cristina

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] error related with too big number of areas?
parts:
Hi Cristina,

20 areas is too many unless you limit the maximum range size
to 2 areas. 20 areas means 2^20 possible geographic ranges
= a state space of 2^20=1,048,576 different states. The
transition matrix is 1048576x1048576=1.099512e+12 which I
think would take more than a gigabyte just to store in
computer memory.

The part of the example script that I post below will be
helpful for planning your analysis.

Your options are:

1. merge areas

2. strong limits on maximum range size

3. Use the BayArea program (Landis et al. 2013), which can
do hundreds of areas, but has no cladogenesis model

4. Explore sparse matrix exponentiation, which can handle
large transition matrices. I have some of this programmed
into BioGeoBEARS/rexpokit, but the resulting calculations
were imprecise so I didn't explore it further. But an
enterprising person with R skillz could explore it further.

Cheers,
Nick

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#toc14
====================================
####################################################
####################################################
# KEY HINT: The number of states (= number of different
possible geographic ranges)
# depends on (a) the number of areas and (b) max_range_size.
# If you have more than about 500-600 states, the
calculations will get REALLY slow,
# since the program has to exponentiate a matrix of e.g.
600x600. Often the computer
# will just sit there and crunch, and never get through the
calculation of the first
# likelihood.
#
# (this is also what is usually happening when LAGRANGE
hangs: you have too many states!)
#
# To check the number of states for a given number of
ranges, try:
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=4, maxareas=4,
include_null_range=TRUE)
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=4, maxareas=4,
include_null_range=FALSE)
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=4, maxareas=3,
include_null_range=TRUE)
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=4, maxareas=2,
include_null_range=TRUE)

# Large numbers of areas have problems:
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=10, maxareas=10,
include_null_range=TRUE)

# ...unless you limit the max_range_size:
numstates_from_numareas(numareas=10, maxareas=2,
include_null_range=TRUE)
####################################################
####################################################
====================================
